title: Psalm 110 (Septuagint) = Psalm 111 (KJV)
description: Psalm 110 in the Septuagint numbering (Psalm 111 in the KJV). Both the manuscript page scan AND the Greek text are taken directly from Codex Sinaiticus (4th century AD) via the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). The Greek transcription preserves the actual uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra abbreviations, and lectional marks of the manuscript. Library folio: 119. English translation verbatim from the King James Version (1611, public domain) via bible-api.com.
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library, with the manuscript text drawn directly from the same source as the scan:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio of Codex Sinaiticus containing this passage, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Library folio reference: 119.
  2. Original text: The verbatim transcription of the Sinaiticus manuscript from the Codex Sinaiticus Project, preserving uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra (e.g. ⟨θϲ⟩ = θεός), and scribal marks. Nomina sacra are shown in angle brackets to indicate the manuscript's sacred-name abbreviations.
  3. English translation: The King James Version (1611), retrieved verbatim from the public-domain bible-api.com endpoint.

Numbering: Codex Sinaiticus follows the Septuagint Psalter, in which this is Psalm 110. In the Hebrew and King James numbering the same psalm is Psalm 111. Verse numbers align between the Greek and the KJV in this psalm. The Greek and English in each section are the same words of the same psalm.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>αλληλουϊαεξομολογηϲομαι ϲοι κε εν ολη καρδια μου εν βουλη ευθιων και ϲυναγωγη <sup>2</sup>μεγαλα τα εργα κυ εξεζητημενα ειϲ παντα τα θεληματα αυτου <sup>3</sup>εξομολογηϲειϲ και μεγαλοπρεπια το εργον αυτου και η δικαιοϲυνη αυτου μενει ειϲ τον αιωνα του αιωνοϲ <sup>4</sup>μνειαν εποιηϲατο των θαυμαϲιων αυτου ελεημων και οικτιρμων ο κϲ <sup>5</sup>τροφην εδωκεν τοιϲ φοβουμενοιϲ αυτον μνηϲθηϲεται ειϲ τον αιωνα διαθηκηϲ αυτου
translation.text:
<sup>1</sup>Praise ye the LORD. I will praise the LORD with
my whole heart, in the assembly of the upright, and
in the congregation. <sup>2</sup>The works of the LORD
are great, sought out of all them that have pleasure therein. <sup>3</sup>His work
is honourable and glorious: and his righteousness endureth for ever. <sup>4</sup>He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered: the LORD
is
 gracious and full of compassion. <sup>5</sup>He hath given meat unto them that fear him: he will ever be mindful of his covenant.

translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>ϊϲχυν εργων εαυτου ανηγγειλεν τω λαω εαυτου του δουναι αυτοιϲ κληρονομιαν εθνων <sup>7</sup>εργα χειρων αυτου αληθια και κριϲιϲ πιϲται παϲαι αι εντολαι αυτου <sup>8</sup>εϲτηριγμεναι ειϲ τον αιωνα του αιωνοϲ πεποιημεναι εν αληθια και ευθυτητι<sup>9</sup>λυτρωϲιν απεϲτιλεν τω λαω αυτου ενετιλατο ειϲ τον αιωνα διαθηκην αυτου αγιον και φοβερον το ονομα αυτου <sup>10</sup>αρχη ϲοφιαϲ φοβοϲ κυ ϲυνεϲιϲ αγαθη παϲι τοιϲ ποιουϲιν αυτην η αινεϲιϲ αυτου μενει ειϲ τον αιωνα του αιωνοϲ
translation.text:
<sup>6</sup>He hath shewed his people the power of his works, that he may give them the heritage of the heathen. <sup>7</sup>The works of his hands
are verity and judgment; all his commandments
are sure. <sup>8</sup>They stand fast for ever and ever,
and are done in truth and uprightness. <sup>9</sup>He sent redemption unto his people: he hath commanded his covenant for ever: holy and reverend
is his name. <sup>10</sup>The fear of the LORD
is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do
his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.

verification.section_folios_note: Each section links to the specific folio(s) containing its verses, resolved per verse via the Codex Sinaiticus Project page index.
